thread:
maria (support): Hey team, customer kevin from AcmePay reporting that when they use our JSON-mode streaming responses their client-side parser gets 'Unexpected end of JSON input'. They included a sample response that stops mid-object.

kevin (customer): This started after last week's deploy. We get a bunch of tokens then the stream ends before the final closing braces. Client throws and our payment flow breaks. Request id: r-9a3b2f.

maria (support): Thanks Kevin — can you paste the raw bytes you received? Also what's your client?

kevin (customer): Attached snippet (trimmed):
```
{"invoices": [{"id": "inv_01","amount": 120.00}, {"id": "inv_02","amount": 90.00}], "summary": {"total": 210.00}, "signature": "abc123",
```
You can see the stream stops after the trailing comma. We use a Node fetch streaming parser.

dylan (eng-runtime): Huh. That looks like the origin stream closed without sending the final '}]}' segments. Two quick checks: is this using transfer-encoding: chunked and did the TCP FIN happen mid-chunk? Any proxys/load balancers?

kevin (customer): Yes: requests go through their API GW then our connection to Redwood (hosted). We saw connection resets in their gateway logs at the same time.

maria (support): Repro attempt logs from our side: I replayed the same prompt with stream: true and capture below. Note the last chunk ended, then connection close within 180ms:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: application/json

7b 22 69 6e 76 6f 69 63 65 73 22 3a ... 2c
<socket closed by peer>
```
That's consistent.

eva (infra): Could be our load balancer health check or keepalive window cutting long-lived connections. Any recent LB config changes?

dylan (eng-runtime): We pushed a streaming buffer change last week (reduces flush frequency). Might interact with chunk boundaries when an upstream proxy has an aggressive idle/tcp timeout. If the final bytes are still in an internal buffer and the proxy closes, client gets partial JSON.

maria (support): Customer says it started after last week's deploy — matches. Kevin, can you switch to non-streaming (single response) temporarily as a workaround?

kevin (customer): We patched to non-streaming and it fixed the parser failures. But throughput matters for us.

dylan (eng-runtime): For a fix we should: 1) add a final explicit flush and sentinel for structured output (e.g. send a final zero-length chunk / explicit close frame so proxies see FIN with empty chunk), 2) add server-side detection of socket close mid-json and emit a log+metric, 3) add guidance in docs for customers to validate tolerant parsing.

maria (support): Filing a bug and escalation — tagging eng-runtime. @dylan can you own a short repro + PR? Include a deterministic script to reproduce with an nginx reverse proxy configured with low proxy_read_timeout.

dylan (eng-runtime): Will do. Quick repro steps I'm using:
1) start nginx with proxy_read_timeout 2s and chunked transfer enabled
2) curl to our streaming endpoint with --no-buffer and write output to file
3) inspect final bytes, compare to expected full JSON

Example curl:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"mode":"json_schema","prompt": "..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams > out.bin
```

I can reproduce locally with LB timeout=1s and our streaming buffer configured to hold final 512 bytes before flush.

kevin (customer): Thanks — will wait for the patch. Appreciate the workaround suggestion.

maria (support): Action items: [dylan] generate repro + PR to flush final chunk and log mid-json closes; [eva] audit LB timeouts in hosted infra (look for recent changes last week); [support] follow up with customer and offer temporary non-stream guidance.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0322-07 — streaming-json-incomplete. Severity: P2.

dylan (eng-runtime): I'll aim for a small PR today to force final chunk flush on structured output endpoints. If we can't guarantee flush due to TCP behavior, we may need to switch to a short-lived single-response fallback for JSON-mode when we detect an upstream proxy between client and server.

eva (infra): I'll roll back the LB tune change from 03/18 and monitor for errors.

maria (support): Thanks all. Kevin — I'll ping you once we have a staging patch. Please let us know if anything else pops up in the meantime. :pray:

kevin (customer): Appreciate it. Patch will be great. :thumbsup:
